decisions.reason: The same message confirms the stainless-steel whisk separately, but the 1500 RPM limit does not change the whisk configuration.
Changing the maximum motor speed does not alter the existing splash-control target or prescribed mitigation methods.
The speed limit is an implementation parameter intended to support mixing quality, but it does not change the required smooth and frothy result.
The source does not change the requirement for simple and reliable event operation.
The 1500 RPM limit does not change bowl capacity, bowl form, refilling policy, or compactness constraints.
Motor mixing speed does not modify the required dispensing flow, froth preservation, or anti-sputtering behavior.
The motor-speed decision may inform later component selection, but it does not change the current requirement to provide a prototype BOM or make any existing BOM requirement attribute stale.
The maximum mixing-motor speed does not change the solenoid mechanism, button actuation, or closed-state dispensing behavior.
The speed limit does not alter the requirement for quickly removable and swappable bowls.
A 1500 RPM operating limit does not necessarily change the 120V wall-powered architecture, and the source specifies no new voltage or power requirement.
The motor-speed limit does not modify bowl or spout cleanability requirements.
The source does not change the requirement to provide system-layout drawings or establish any specific layout alteration.
